summary.headline: Marico Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 23% and EBITDA/PAT up 25%, with India volume up 11% and FY27 guidance of 20% EBITDA growth.
summary.overview: Marico reported a very strong Q1 FY27 with consolidated revenue up 23% and EBITDA and PAT up 25%, its highest profit growth in 28 quarters, on top of a high base. India business grew 11% in volume and 21% in revenue, with Parachute Rigids volume up 10% and VAHO value up 22%. Gross margin expanded 30 bps and EBITDA margin rose 40 bps to 20.7%, even as A&P grew 25%. Management raised confidence in FY27 (revenue above INR15,000 crore, EBITDA growth high-teens aiming for 20%) but flagged higher crude-linked and edible oil input costs from Q2.

segments.name: India - Parachute Rigids
segments.commentary: Volume up 10%, strongest in 20 quarters, with over 400 bps volume share gain; revenue up 23% on anniversarisation of prior price increases and a one-time ~10% price cut on loyalty packs.

segments.name: India - VAHO (value-added hair oils)
segments.commentary: Value up 22%, led by mid and premium hair oils (high-teens volume growth); almond oil targeted at INR100 crore ARR by FY28.

segments.name: India - Saffola Edible Oil
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7% on calibrated pricing; high single-digit volume decline from rationalising select variants to protect threshold profitability.

segments.name: Foods (incl. 4700BC, Cosmix)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 43%, annualised run rate above INR1,300 crore; ex-acquisitions growth is in double digits.

segments.name: Premium Personal Care
segments.commentary: Annualised revenue run rate of around INR450 crore; shampoo targeting ~INR100 crore revenue this year after national launch.

segments.name: Digital-first brands (Beardo, Plix, Cosmix, 4700BC)
segments.commentary: ARR above INR1,100 crore; Beardo at double-digit profitability, Plix high single digit trending to double digit; Plix at ~INR800 crore.

segments.name: International - Vietnam
segments.commentary: Constant currency growth 27%, driven by male and female personal care.

segments.name: International - MENA
segments.commentary: Growth 24%, with Gulf and Egypt both performing well despite inflation and operating challenges in the Gulf.

segments.name: International - Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Constant currency growth 4%, hit by pricing anniversarisation, demand softness from high inflation and fuel price spikes.

segments.name: International - South Africa and new country/export
segments.commentary: South Africa grew 8% (hair care led by Black Chic, Just for Kids, Isoplus); new country development and exports grew 16%.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Core business growth above 50%; about 5% of India revenue excluding digital brands; all digital channels above 20% of India revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue growth in double digits, crossing INR15,000 crore; management says this is achievable 'easily'.
FY27 EBITDA growth high-teens as base case, aspiring to 20%; reverse math implies EBITDA margin expansion of about 140-150 bps YoY if INR15,000 crore is delivered.
FY27 India volume growth high single digit; international constant currency growth mid-teens.
Another double-digit India volume quarter targeted within the next three quarters.
Copra expected range-bound around 30-35% below last year's peak, with a slight upward bias; crude and vegetable oils trending up, so input costs seen higher in Q2.
Gross margin: intent to hold the percentage, but quarterly guidance difficult given LP/polymer costs up 60-70%.
Effective tax rate guided ~18% for FY27 and ~19-20% for FY28.
Vision 2030: INR20,000 crore revenue with mid-teens EBITDA CAGR.
Digital portfolio: path to profitability for other brands over the next 12-18 months; target of INR4,000 crore revenue at early-teens EBITDA margin by 2030.
capex_capacity: Acquisitions of 4700BC and Cosmix are capital outlay and do not constrain A&P spend, per management.
AI-led demand sensing and supply chain investment cited as lowering distributor pipeline stock, speeding price-drop pass-through.
Project SETU general trade route-to-market now rolled out in India and Vietnam; direct distribution and technology investments ongoing.
Shampoo launched nationally; almond oil and cold-pressed oil named as big bets with critical mass targeted soon.
Cold-pressed oil expected to become a sizable portion of Saffola business by next year, with margins far above core Saffola edible oil.
demand_pricing: Parachute: one price cut of ~10% taken in Q4 FY26 on loyalty packs only; small and price-point packs untouched; no further price action planned as off-season approaches.

Parachute volume growth attributed to deeper loyalty-pack price cuts (reducing downtrading), supply chain advantage over small players, faster price-drop execution and more rational organised competitors; management called 10% an aberration and reiterated mid-single-digit Parachute volume guidance.
No grammage increase in the INR10/INR20 price-point packs cut last year; the volume growth is organic.
Input costs: LP and polymers up 60-70% on crude; edible oil prices rising; price increases not fully passed on to consumers.
Quick commerce is a channel-pack architecture exercise to avoid cannibalisation; modern trade and marketplace e-commerce growth has slowed relative to the past.
Competition in plant protein and ACV (Plix, Cosmix): management views 2-3 players as useful for category build; Plix pivoting to premium personal care.
Saffola entry-point variants are commoditised and being pruned; Saffola Gold unaffected by cold-pressed competition; mid-single-digit Saffola volume growth considered acceptable.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing power and competitive intensity in plant protein, collagen and ACV (Plix, Cosmix)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said D2C LTV/CAC and repeat rates are healthy; competition is acceptable for category building, and Plix and Cosmix will not be confined to protein and ACV, with Cosmix at a mid-to-high-teens margin at acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Can almond hair oil reach INR100 crore by FY28 and what about 4700BC and Cosmix versus plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees room for disruption of a leader earning super-normal profit, citing its Amla playbook and SETU distribution; both 4700BC and Cosmix are tracking well and are expected to end the year ahead of initial assumptions.

qa_highlights.question: Parachute price decline outlook and copra risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Total price cut was ~10% on loyalty packs only; copra expected range-bound at 30-35% below peak; only one price drop, no further pricing action; decent volume growth expected in the next one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How to reconcile gross margin and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin likely to be held but gains from copra offset by crude-linked LP/polymer and edible oil costs; full-year reverse math implies 140-150 bps EBITDA margin expansion for INR15,000 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10% Parachute volume growth organic, and is India 11% like-for-like?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; no grammage changes, 11% India volume is organic and excludes 4700BC and Cosmix; 10% called an aberration against mid-single-digit guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is A&P growing only 9% at consolidated level, and what about the tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said A&P grew 25% in the quarter, funded from cost tailwinds and acquisitions being capital outlay; tax rate ~17.5% this quarter, guided ~18% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for VAHO and Saffola volume decline risk?
qa_highlights.answer: VAHO mid-and-premium volume up high teens with double-digit trajectory expected and high-teens targeted; Saffola mid-single-digit volume growth considered fine as it pivots toward food.

risks_watch: Crude-linked LP/polymer costs up 60-70% and higher edible oil prices expected to weigh on Q2 input costs and gross margin.
Copra has an upward bias after correction; any reversal could pressure the Parachute price cushion.
Saffola volume: high single-digit decline; entry-point variant pruning and cold-pressed competition.
Bangladesh growth slowed to 4% constant currency due to inflation and fuel costs; Gulf inflation and operating challenges.
Digital brands: profitability targets rely on 12-18 month timelines; competitive pressure in plant protein and ACV from private labels and e-commerce players.
Shampoo and almond oil scale-up ambitions (INR100 crore each) are unproven against entrenched leaders.
Modern trade and marketplace e-commerce growth has slowed relative to past quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter and FY27 targets, with explicit caution on Q2 input costs and gross margin, which management declined to guide quarterly. Some answers on Parachute volume sustainability and the almond and shampoo ambitions were framed as aspirations, not commitments.
key_quotes: We have started the year on a very strong note with a consolidated revenue growth of 23% and EBITDA and PAT growth of 25%, making our highest profit growth in the last 28 quarters.
And the total drop was around 10%. Now we were clear that we will take only one drop.
Yes, 10% is an aberration. We don't really expect ourselves to keep delivering high single digit or 10% volume growth for the year.
The assets that we have bought are capital outlay. So that does not impact our ability to invest behind the A&P line items.
So just on the guidance side, very difficult to give on gross margin because we believe it will be a little bit of mix of both, but we would try and hold the gross margin percentage.

adds.what: Cold-pressed oil expansion within Saffola (no plant or capacity figure given)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to cross INR15,000 crore (double-digit growth) and EBITDA growth of high-teens aspiring to 20%, backed mainly by Parachute and VAHO volume/value momentum, a ~10% loyalty-pack price cut and digital brands, with no specific capacity additions or order numbers quantified.
